method: Real patent documents. Every structure was located by reading the PDF - pdftotext -layout for text, pdfimages -png to pull the embedded structure clippings at their native resolution (which is almost always better than re-rendering the page), and pdftoppm at 200-450 dpi where a wedge had to be settled. Each resolved molecule required TWO INDEPENDENT VIEWS to agree: a PubChem record reached either by a NAME printed in the document (INN, development code, or full IUPAC name) or, where the document prints no name, by a PUG-REST /compound/smiles/ structure search on the drawn reading, AND a reading of the drawing itself. A structure search was accepted only when the returned record's InChIKey equalled the RDKit InChIKey of the hand reading exactly; a returned CID with a different key was treated as a MISS, not a match. Every SMILES round-trips through RDKit and its InChIKey was recomputed with RDKit; the builder that wrote this file asserts inchikey == inchikey_rdkit for every row and refuses a molecules[] entry without a PubChem CID. WHERE A COMPOUND IS A CLOSE VARIANT OF A CATALOGUED DRUG, its SMILES was DERIVED FROM THAT DRUG'S PubChem RECORD by changing only the substituent in question, rather than re-drawn by hand, so that shared stereocentres keep a provenance instead of being re-guessed. That discipline caught two errors during this round, both recorded in the notes.
excluded: Rows with no SMILES are NOT in molecules[]. score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry and a None raises TypeError before its own error message, so Markush/R-group generics (generic: true), structures with no second independent view (confidence: unresolved), and compounds that are named in the text but never drawn all live in a sibling per-group unscoreable array, which the scorer ignores. Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row. A row also requires a PubChem CID: every molecules[] entry in every previous round carries one, and this round keeps that invariant - a compound whose structure is certain but which PubChem does not hold (cefiderocol sodium, pritelivir maleate, two molnupiravir acetonide esters, nirmatrelvir's C31) is unresolved, not scoreable.
count_caveat: structures_drawn counts DEPICTIONS on the KEPT pages of each extract, not on the whole grant, and is flagged structures_drawn_is_estimate: true in six groups where it was counted from image objects or a low-dpi contact sheet rather than box by box. No estimated number can move a score: recall runs over molecules[] and precision over what a pipeline emits, and both are exact. SEVEN GROUPS SHOULD BE SCORED RECALL-ONLY because most of what they draw is deliberately uncatalogued: EP3720438B1_gwt1_antifungals, EP3578557B1_cipargamin, EP3473629B1_baloxavir_route, EP3299356B1_pleuromutilin, EP3512863B1_ethynyl_nucleosides, EP3810115B1_manogepix_prodrugs and EP3743419B1_antiparasitic_tetrazoles. TWO GROUPS SCORE ZERO BY DESIGN and are false-positive tests only: EP3643719B1_spiropyrimidinetriones and EP4061375B1_antimalarial_markush.

molecules.name: taniborbactam

molecules.basis: The full chemical name is printed at [0005] and repeated in every claim: '(R)-3-(2-(trans-4-(2-aminoethylamino)cyclohexyl)acetamido)-2-hydroxy-3,4-dihydro-2H-benzo[e][1,2]oxaborinine-8-carboxylic acid'. molecules.note: SILENT STEREO NORMALISATION - the most dangerous thing in this group. The document says trans-4-cyclohexyl in words AND draws it trans (hashed + bold). PubChem CID 76902493 does NOT encode the cyclohexane at all: its own InChIKey is PFZUWUXKQPRWAL-PXCJXSSVSA-N (undefined). Submitting the trans-specified SMILES (PFZUWUXKQPRWAL-BJJXKVORSA-N) to PUG-REST /compound/smiles/ returns CID 76902493 anyway, with nothing in the response saying the query carried stereochemistry the record does not. So a FAITHFUL reading of this drawing scores stereo, not exact, against this reference, and a tool that drops the cyclohexane wedges scores exact. That is a property of the reference, not of the prediction.
